transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a proposed securitization of $30 million in trade receivables through a newly formed SPV, with a 3% dilution reserve and ordinary seller support permitted. The proposed funding date is November 20, 2026. Before I finalize approval, I'd like to follow our standard pre-closing routine. Could the risk analyst and finance counsel please report any transaction-specific issues they've identified? I want to make sure we've covered all bases before I sign off on the final operating conditions.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Maya, I need to flag a significant issue. My review of the October collections file, completed yesterday and still in my working paper pending the monthly risk-pack circulation, shows 6% historical dilution rather than the 3% assumed in the draft. Our risk methodology therefore requires an 8% dilution reserve. Additionally, $4,000,000 of the receivables are affiliate balances that must be excluded, leaving an eligible pool of exactly $26,000,000 — not $30,000,000. These findings materially affect the transaction structure and the reserve assumptions.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Maya, I need to raise two critical issues from the transaction counsel memo I received this morning. First, the structure only qualifies as a true sale if the seller has no recourse for ordinary obligor credit losses — but our draft transaction currently permits ordinary seller support, which would jeopardize true-sale treatment. Second, a UCC financing statement must be perfected before the November 20, 2026 funding date. Both of these must be resolved before closing.
transcript.speaker: A3
